history.summary: Baseline (unmodified fork). Verbose output showed ALL 5 detected font-variant prefixes classified 'mono' -- entire deck (Helvetica Neue + Menlo) rendered as Consolas monospace in the PPTX. Root cause: _analyze_glyphs() in typst_svg_parser.py marked any glyph prefix using quadratic Bezier curves (SVG 'Q' commands) as 'mono'. Quadratic curves are a property of the TrueType glyf outline FORMAT, not of monospace-ness -- virtually every macOS/Windows font (proportional or mono) is TrueType, so this heuristic false-positived on 100% of prefixes.

Fix 1: replaced quadratic-curve mono detection with a real metric signal -- glyph advance-width uniformity, measured directly from consecutive <use x=...> offsets within a typst-text run (normalized per-run, pooled across runs, classified mono if coefficient-of-variation < 0.12 with >=8 samples). typst_svg_parser.py: _analyze_glyphs() now always defaults style='regular'; new _collect_advance_deltas()/_is_monospace_prefix() helpers; _prescan_font_variants() Step 1 rewritten to use them. Verified: font style mapping went from {all 5: mono} to 2 correctly-mono (Menlo Regular/Bold) + 3 correctly-non-mono (Helvetica Neue Regular/Bold/MediumItalic) prefixes -- exact match to `pdffonts` on the ground-truth PDF (5 font resources).

Fix 2: _font_variant_to_props() in converter.py hardcoded 'Arial' (regular/bold/italic) and 'Consolas' (mono) regardless of ConversionConfig -- default_latin_font/default_cs_font existed on the config dataclass but were never wired into this function. Added default_mono_font field, threaded self.config.default_latin_font/default_mono_font through both call sites, added typ2pptx --latin-font/--mono-font CLI flags. Root cause note: typst.ts's rich SVG artifact carries ZERO font-family metadata anywhere (verified empirically: 0 matches for /font-family/ across a real 443KB artifact SVG; foreignObject <h5:div> overlays carry only font-size, for text-selection, not family) -- so the real family name can only come from a caller who knows it out-of-band (e.g. the brand.json that drove the original Typst compile), which these new flags now allow.

Fix 3: with mono no longer masking everything, discovered a second real bug: the pre-existing Step 3 bold/italic/bolditalic classifier ranked purely by glyph advance-width ratio vs the regular prefix, which SWAPPED Helvetica Neue Bold (labeled 'italic') and Helvetica Neue Medium Italic (labeled 'bold') on this exact document -- Medium Italic happened to measure wider than Bold for this deck's character set. Added a second, independent axis: glyph slant, estimated by linear-regression slope of (x,y) path coordinates pooled per prefix (x = m*y + b); italic is a uniform horizontal shear so real italic faces show a slope far outside the document's own upright baseline (measured +0.14 for the real italic vs -0.02 to -0.06 for every upright weight here). New _get_glyph_slant()/_prefix_avg_slant() + _SLANT_ITALIC_THRESHOLD=0.08; Step 3 rewritten to combine independent bold-by-width and italic-by-slant flags instead of one 1-D ranking. Verified via python-pptx run dump on slide 11 (the deck's only italic text, a pull-quote): bold/italic now correctly assigned to headings vs quote respectively (previously inverted).

Fix 4 (extension of fix 1+3): the mono bucket still collapsed ALL mono prefixes into one style, losing Menlo Regular vs Menlo Bold distinction (kickers/index-badges set in mono weight 600-800 rendered non-bold). Added Step 4 in _prescan_font_variants: sub-classify prefixes already tagged 'mono' using the same width-ratio+slant two-axis method against the most-used mono prefix, producing mono/monobold/monoitalic/monobolditalic. Wired into _font_variant_to_props (converter.py). Verified via python-pptx dump across slides 1/4/11: kicker text ('CONFIDENTIAL...', 'THREE IDEAS'), index badges ('01'/'02'/'03' in three-pillars boxes) now correctly Menlo bold=True; body labels (PRESENTER/DATE/DOC, pagination '01/08') correctly Menlo bold=False. Full pytest suite: 201 passed, 184 skipped, 1 pre-existing unrelated failure (TestQuerySpeakerNotes, needs the real typst-ts-cli binary this sandbox can't download -- confirmed failing identically on the unmodified pre-fix code via git stash).

Real-pipeline validation (outer loop, not the sandboxed subagent): re-ran the SAME example (bdg2-pitch/dfdf/19-brutalist-blocknumeral) through our actual production pipeline -- real typst-ts-cli binary, real brand.json (dfdf: display+body both resolve to real family 'Helvetica Neue', mono 'Menlo'), real soffice (which the subagent's sandbox could not reach at all -- its own compare_pdf_pptx.py runs hung indefinitely there). CONFIRMED font fixes hold up for real: `Font style mapping` on this deck now shows a genuine mix (bold/mono/monobold/regular/bolditalic) instead of everything=mono, and visual inspection of page 1 and page 5 confirms correct font family/weight/style throughout -- fonts are FIXED, verified end-to-end, not just in the subagent's reconstructed sandbox test.

BUT pixel-diff (finally run for real, since soffice only works outside the subagent's sandbox) surfaced a SECOND, separate, systemic bug the font fix didn't touch: a geometry/scale mismatch. On every page, everything to the right of the layout's vertical divider line renders visibly LARGER and shifted rightward in the PPTX vs the ground-truth PDF, and the drift magnitude grows with x-coordinate (not a flat offset -- a genuine scale-factor mismatch). Most visible on the decorative numeral glyphs (e.g. page 5's giant '05' -- the '5' half extends much further right and is noticeably bigger in the pptx) and on body text size. Aspect ratio of the two renders is nearly identical (1.7778 pdf vs 1.7751 pptx) so this isn't a comparison-tool resize artifact -- it's real. Overall diff stats for this example: mean_abs_diff=22.8, max_pct_pixels_changed=25.6% (all 12 pages), driven mostly by this, not by fonts anymore. Strong prior: this repo's own pre-fork history has a commit '9867d58 feat: pair geometry EMU scale with a configurable font-size scale' -- i.e. the maintainers already knew geometry-EMU-scale and font-size-scale could drift out of sync; worth reading that commit and the current --emu-per-px / font_size_scale wiring in converter.py + drawingml_utils.py to see if the pairing is incomplete, or if a DIFFERENT scale is applied to shape x/width vs text x/size.

Adversarial self-review of the font fixes (iterations 1-4), run per the standard post-turn review gate. Did NOT re-touch font classification logic per iteration 5's note above except for one confirmed real bug found below -- geometry/scale drift is a separate, untouched concern. Since the sandboxed environment still can't reach soffice/real typst-ts-cli, built a SECOND, network-independent verification data point: tests/typ_sources/synth_font_variants.typ, a minimal fixture (no @preview package imports, unlike the repo's existing basic_text.typ which needs touying and could not be compiled in this sandbox either -- packages.typst.org is also outside the sandbox's network allowlist) covering all 6 font_variant styles directly. This fixture FAILED on first run: mono detection produced 0 pooled advance-width deltas for 5 of 6 prefixes (including the genuinely monospace one), so mono text rendered in the latin font instead of the mono font. Root cause: _collect_advance_deltas() treated ANY <use> glyph reference missing from glyph_defs as fatal and discarded the entire text group's deltas -- and verified directly against the raw SVG that a <use href=#goGLyhgM> id (etc) recurs at word-length intervals with NO defining element anywhere in the document: Typst omits the empty-ink glyph outline for spaces but still emits the <use x=...> for text-flow positioning, so almost every real sentence hits this. Fixed: a missing-glyph <use> now contributes its x-offset to neighboring deltas without setting or breaking the group's prefix-consistency check, instead of aborting the group. Re-verified BOTH the synthetic fixture (now correctly detects mono/monobold) and the original real deck (byte-identical font-style classification output before/after -- no regression, since that deck's mono/display runs happened to be short label text mostly free of internal spaces, which is exactly why this bug didn't surface during the earlier iterations' verification). Committed separately (fd4c233) with the fixture checked in as a lasting regression test. One residual, NOT fixed (pre-existing in the original width-ratio-for-bold logic, not introduced by this session): a real Helvetica Neue Italic face's glyph outlines measured wider than Regular's for the synthetic fixture's text, so pure italic got a false bold=True flag (bolditalic instead of italic) -- a font/threshold-specific edge case in the pre-existing bold-by-width heuristic, distinct from the swap bug fixed in iteration 3.

Root-caused the geometry drift from iteration 5: NOT a code bug in the fork. typ2pptx's font_size_scale defaults to 0.75 (correct for CSS-px-at-96dpi SVG sources) but our typst.ts artifacts are pt-true (1 SVG unit = 1pt, viewBox matches the page size in typst pt -- confirmed: PDF page size 959.976x540pt == 13.333x7.5in exactly). The maintainers had ALREADY documented this exact case in commit 9867d58's message and shipped --font-size-scale/--emu-per-px flags for it -- we just weren't passing --font-size-scale 1.0. Without it: slide came out 10x5.625in (0.75x too small) instead of 13.333x7.5in. With it: slide size is exactly correct (verified: 12192000x6858000 EMU == 13.333x7.5in exactly) and the giant decorative numeral no longer overlaps the title text -- visually confirmed via direct PNG comparison, composition now matches the ground-truth PDF. Pixel diff score barely moved (22.8 -> 22.8) despite the clear visual fix, because remaining diff is now dominated by inherent cross-renderer text anti-aliasing/baseline noise (Typst's rasterizer vs LibreOffice's) that flags ~100% of a thin glyph's pixels for a 2-3px shift even when visually negligible -- exactly the calibration caveat given to the first subagent iteration. Pixel score alone is not a reliable metric for this class of fix; visual inspection is.

CONCLUSION: the fork's actual bugs (font classification, hardcoded family names) are fixed. The remaining piece is CALLER-SIDE: our own generation pipeline must always pass --font-size-scale 1.0 (since we only ever feed it typst.ts pt-true SVGs) and --latin-font/--mono-font per persona (real names from brand.json). Known remaining limitation, not fixed this round: --latin-font is ONE flag for all non-mono text, so a persona whose display font differs from its body font (e.g. bdg2: Cormorant Garamond display vs Inter body) will still collapse both to one family in the PPTX. For dfdf (this test persona) display and body both resolve to the same real family (Helvetica Neue) so this limitation didn't show up here -- needs a spot-check against a persona where they genuinely differ before calling this fully done.

diff_stats.note: score misleading here -- see summary; visual check is the real signal for this fix

notes: Environment note: this sandbox could not reach the typst-ts-cli GitHub release binary (proxy blocks the release-assets.githubusercontent.com redirect target) and could not read the worktree-local font dir or the pip-installed typ2pptx's bundled binary (outside the sandbox's granted read paths). Worked around by using the @myriaddreamin/typst-ts-node-compiler npm package (same underlying Rust compiler typst-ts-cli wraps) via a small Node script to compile layout.typ -> rich SVG artifact (NodeCompiler.svg()), and macOS system fonts (/System/Library/Fonts, which already has Helvetica Neue + Menlo) instead of the custom brand font dir. brand.json for the 'dfdf' persona was reconstructed from `pdffonts` on the ground-truth ../19-brutalist-blocknumeral.pdf (5 embedded font resources: HelveticaNeue, HelveticaNeue-Bold, HelveticaNeue-MediumItalic, Menlo-Regular, Menlo-Bold) since the real brand JSON path given wasn't in this sandbox's readable scope either.

Visual pixel-diff via tools/compare_pdf_pptx.py could not be completed in this sandbox: soffice --headless --convert-to pdf hangs indefinitely (XPC 'Connection Invalid' errors against com.apple.hiservices-xpcservice, likely a macOS accessibility service unreachable from the sandboxed environment) and never produces output, even with a scratch -env:UserInstallation profile. Verification was instead done structurally: python-pptx run-level font.name/bold/italic dumps against the deck's known ground truth (pdffonts on the reference PDF + the .typ source's explicit font/weight/style calls), which is arguably more precise for font-identity verification than a pixel heatmap anyway, at the cost of not confirming overall visual layout fidelity.

Residual known imperfection: the deck's one italic run (a medium-weight pull quote, HelveticaNeue-MediumItalic) gets bold=True+italic=True in the PPTX, not italic-only, because its advance width also measured >1.05x regular (medium weight is somewhat wider, not just slanted). PPTX's binary bold/italic model has no 'medium weight' concept, so this is a real vocabulary limitation, not obviously fixable without a step change (e.g. emitting a real font substitution to a specific medium-weight face) -- flagged rather than fixed.

NEXT: fonts are done -- do not re-touch font classification logic without a strong reason. Focus entirely on the geometry/scale drift. Regenerate via the real pipeline (see README section 'Regenerating a deck through the LOCAL fork' in the fix-loop task history / prior agent instructions) -- typst-ts-cli + real font-path + real brand/content json all resolve fine outside the sandbox; soffice also works fine outside the sandbox, so tools/compare_pdf_pptx.py can be used directly this time.
